title: Nurturing Local Startups and Talent in Electronic Game Development and E-sports
what_it_is: Nurturing Local Startups and Talent in Electronic Game Development and E-sports

sections.label: E-sports startup support measures
sections.summary: Asks what measures nurture local electronic game and E-sports startups and talent, and their results, noting global and Singapore revenue figures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leon Perera
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Trade and Industry (a) what measures are being taken to nurture local startups and talent in electronic game development and E-sports; and (b) what results have been associated with these efforts to date.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: They generated over US$140 billion globally in 2018, of which almost half was from the Asia Pacific region.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: In Singapore, the development and distribution of video games contributed S$1.95 billion in 2017.

sections.label: Startup SG support initiative
sections.summary: Startup SG, launched in 2017, gives local companies financial and non-financial support including mentorship and startup capital via Startup SG Founder.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Launched in 2017, the Startup SG initiative provides local companies a range of financial and non-financial support, such as mentorship and startup capital support through the Startup SG Founder programme.

sections.label: Singapore hosting Gamescom Asia
sections.summary: Singapore will host the first Asian edition of Gamescom in 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Trade and Industry (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Singapore will also host the first Asian edition of Gamescom in 2020.

sections.label: No picking industry winners
sections.summary: Public money is used without choosing winners and losers, which is not how industries are developed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: In general, I would state this: we are using public money, we are not in the business of choosing winners and losers, and that is not the way we develop our industries.

sections.label: Market failure before spending
sections.summary: Government spending of public money requires careful asking of where the market failure being addressed is.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Whenever we spend Government money, which is actually the public's money, then we have to be very careful and ask ourselves this question: where is the market failure that we are trying to address?

sections.label: Monitoring gaming addiction disorders
sections.summary: Asks about combating gaming disorders and addiction alongside E-sports, with MSF and NAMS monitoring the issue.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I am just wondering, just like the way we were developing the casinos, what are we doing here in terms of combating gaming disorders and addiction, as we alongside develop this e-sports area?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: So, this is where the Ministry of Social and Family Development, together with the National Addictions Management Service or what we call NAMS, is working closely to monitor this issue.

sections.label: Investing in addiction prevention
sections.summary: The passage states that for many addictions, investing resources in prevention is better than only managing issues after they arise.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chan Chun Sing
sentences.text: Like many of these addictions, the best thing for us is to invest our resources in prevention rather than just post-issue management.
